cards.explanation: The answer is four chariots. Zechariah lifts up his eyes and sees "…four chariots coming out from between two mountains—mountains of bronze." Zechariah is the prophet who has been getting these visions. Four chariots at once is a lot of traffic for one pair of mountains, and I bet he stood there with his mouth open.
The answer is True. The text says the horses were red, black, white and dappled, "…all of them strong." Not one weak team in the bunch, friends. That's a lineup I'd be proud to have in my bakery.

The answer is that he asks the angel what they are. Zechariah says to the angel who was speaking with him, "What are these, my lord?" He doesn't pretend to understand and he doesn't wander off. He just asks. I wish I had done more of that in my own early days, instead of nodding at everything like I knew what was going on.

The answer is their station before the Lord. The angel says, "These are the four spirits of heaven, going forth from their station before the Lord of all the earth." So they start out standing in the Lord's presence, friends. That tells you who they answer to.

The answer is south. The angel says, "…the one with the dappled horses toward the south." Black horses go north, white horses go west, and dappled horses go south. That's three directions out of four, and the red horses' direction isn't spelled out in these verses.

The answer is False. The LORD does not tell the horses to wait at the mountains. The horses were "…eager to go and patrol the earth…" and the LORD said, "…Go and patrol the earth." So they patrolled the earth. When the Lord says go, they go.

The answer is the LORD's. The LORD summons Zechariah and says, "…those going to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north." He's the one speaking, so it's His Spirit. The word is "My," friends, and that settles it.
